subject: history
title: Revolutions: Cause and Effect
welcome_lead: Today you'll trace what caused each revolution and what changed afterwards.
meta_desc: GCSE History Revolutions causes and consequences — American, French, Russian.
final_note: You can now explain the causes and consequences of each of the three revolutions.

walkthroughs.body_html:
After 1763 Britain taxed the colonies to pay for war debts.

The Stamp Act, Tea Act and Boston Massacre fed resentment. By 1775 fighting broke out at Lexington. The result was a new republic with a written Constitution by 1787.

France's three Estates were unequal — clergy and nobles paid no tax. Bread prices soared in 1788-89.

The Bastille fell on 14 July 1789. The Declaration of the Rights of Man followed. But the Reign of Terror under Robespierre showed revolution can devour its own.

Tsar Nicholas II refused real reform after 1905. WWI brought military disaster and food shortages.

The February 1917 revolution made a weak Provisional Government. It kept fighting Germany — fatal. Lenin's promise of 'Peace, Bread, Land' won support and the Bolsheviks seized power in October.

No taxation without representation
Workers of the world unite

Thousands guillotined 1793-94
Napoleon's empire

mcqs.q: What happened in the Russian Revolution of 1917?
options: The Bolsheviks overthrew the Tsar in 1917.
There were two revolutions: February overthrew the Tsar and installed the Provisional Government; October saw the Bolsheviks seize power from that government.
Vesalius invented the microscope.
Lenin personally led the storming of the Winter Palace.

mcqs.q: Why was Vesalius significant in the history of medicine?
options: Vesalius invented the microscope.
Vesalius discovered the cause of disease and ended humoral theory.
His 1543 De Humani Corporis Fabrica corrected Galen's errors via human dissection and accurate illustration, founding modern anatomy though not curing disease.
Lenin personally led the storming of the Winter Palace.

mcqs.q: Why was the NHS founded in 1948?
options: The NHS was founded in 1918 after the influenza pandemic.
The NHS was founded because Churchill wanted to thank soldiers after WWII.
Beveridge's 1942 report identified disease as a 'giant evil'; Labour's 1945 manifesto promised universal healthcare; Bevan unified hospitals and made care free at point of use.
Vesalius invented the microscope.
